title: Rav Chanina (or Chinena) of Sura
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Ketubot 63b it is told that the mother of R' Chanina of Sura was rebellious against her husband, and Mar Zutra compelled her, and R' Chanina of Sura was born from her. Hyman concludes that this Mar Zutra is without doubt Mar Zutra Rabba, who is mentioned in Beitzah 8a: "Mar Zutra expounded in the name of Mar Zutra Rabba." For Mar Zutra, the colleague of Rav Ashi, was also a colleague of R-Ch of Sura, as in Menachot 31b [supplied; named parallel at 31a]: Rav Ashi said, "Mar Zutra told me: Rabbi Chanina of Sura raised a difficulty" (and in Sefer ha-Dorot he did not notice this). And in Niddah 66a [supplied; consulted passage at 67b–68a] Mar Zutra prohibits while Rav Chinena of Sura permits. Rav Ada said to Rav Chinena of Sura: "Was it not so? There was an incident involving the wife of Abba Mari the Exilarch, who was angry; R-N bar Yitzchak went to appease her," etc.
He is mentioned in halakhic discussion in Berakhot 52b and Shabbat 23b.

Hyman continues: He said, "What reason is he stating?"; and in Ketubot 99b; Sotah 25a he said, "Come, hear"; and in Sotah 2b he said: let a person not say to his wife nowadays, "Do not seclude yourself"; and in Kiddushin 79a he said, "Who taught 'the barrel'? R-M"; and in Bava Batra 136a Rav Pappi objects to his words; and in Zevachim 85b he disputes with Rav Mari; and in Avodah Zarah 18b he said, "He bought and sold, א״כ [unresolved; the named parallel has ‘that is the difference’]," and there 47b; and in Chullin 136a he said, "These rules do not exist." And in Sefer ha-Dorot he wrote that Sefer ha-Yuchasin forgot his memory, but it is found in the complete Yuchasin in its place.

notes.text: Chanina/Chinena, Rav/Rabbi and Hyman’s earlier-versus-later Mar Zutra argument are preserved. The compressed Menachot difficulty and the Avodah Zarah fragment נשא ונתן א״כ still need matching connected passages.
The sotah quotation concerns a husband’s warning about seclusion. Hyman explicitly presents the identification of the earlier Mar Zutra as certain; the compressed source passages still need checking.

The whole consulted Beitzah 8a paragraph has Mar Zutra expounding in the name of Mar Zutra Rabba; it does not independently establish Hyman’s certain identification of the earlier figure. Ketubot 63b has the compelled woman and the birth of Rabbi Chanina of Sura, followed by a qualification about heavenly assistance; that continuation is not inserted into Hyman’s abridgment. The quoted hair-washing dispute and Abba Mari’s wife occur in the whole consulted Niddah 67b ending and 68a continuation, beside Hyman’s supplied 66a: Mar Zutra forbids, Rav Chinnana of Sura permits, Rav Adda questions him, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak goes to appease her. The whole Kiddushin 79a paragraph reads Rav Chanina “of Syria” and Rabbi Shimon, beside the supplied Sura and unresolved R-M; the siglum is not silently expanded to Rabbi Meir. Menachot 31a and Avodah Zarah 18b supply the previously noted comparisons, without repairing Hyman’s 31b or א״כ. His criticism of Sefer HaDorot and report about complete Yuchasin remain his bibliographical claims, not independently collated editions or global absence findings.
